title: Remote Access Security Act
committees: Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee
last_action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
status: Passed House; referred to Senate Banking
summary: Would extend the Export Control Reform Act to remote access by foreign persons—including access through the internet or cloud computing services—when the covered item could pose a serious national-security or foreign-policy risk. The change would let the Commerce Department license and enforce controls on remote access to controlled technology, closing a pathway that can provide foreign users access to advanced computing without a physical export.
committee_dynamics: The House passed the amended bill 369-22 under suspension of the rules. Its large bipartisan vote and referral to Senate Banking give it a materially stronger position than most standalone technology-control bills, although Senate action is still required.
advance_rationale: Overwhelming House passage and a direct national-security rationale make further action comparatively plausible, but the bill has not advanced in the Senate.
verification_level: Bill details updated from Congress.gov on 2026-10-30.
